# Best Power Station and Solar Combos for an RV

The right pick depends mostly on one question: **do you need to run the roof air conditioner off battery?** A 13,500 BTU AC draws about 1,500W while running and over 3,000W at compressor startup, so a ~1,000W unit won't start it ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

## If you want to run the AC or boondock full-time

**EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** is the top RV pick in my results.
- 4,096Wh of capacity, expandable past 12kWh.
- 4,000W continuous output with 8,000W surge.
- Recharges 0–80% from a wall outlet in about 50 minutes.
- Under 30 dBA at low load, so it's fine during campground quiet hours.
- A TT-30 dogbone adapter connects it to your shore power inlet.
- Downsides: it takes two people to lift, and it's the most expensive option here.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** is the simpler alternative.
- 3,024Wh capacity, 3,000W continuous output, 6,000W surge.
- Enough to start a roof AC without adding a soft-start kit.
- Source: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**ALLPOWERS R4000** is the budget big-battery option with an active deal.
- 3,456Wh LiFePO4 battery and 3,600W output on US 120V. The "4,000W" in the name is the 230V rating.
- It has an RV outlet.
- It accepts 2,000W of solar, but only if you use all three inputs, since each one maxes out at 650W.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb).
- Price is $1,499. Code **EXTRA12** takes off $179.88, bringing it to **$1,319.12**. The code expires Nov 15, 2026, and was tested in the store's cart on Oct 23.
- **Return caveat:** ALLPOWERS's refund page says sale items can't be returned, and this unit is listed well below its $3,299 list price.
- Warranty is 5 years.
- Buy: https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh. This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

## If you don't need AC (fridge, lights, laptop, fans, Starlink)

**BLUETTI AC200L** is a strong mid-range value.
- 2,048Wh capacity and 2,400W output.
- Built-in 30A RV port.
- 1,200W solar input, which is good for a rooftop array.
- Sources: [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- Get the AC200L, not the older AC200P. The AC200P is capped at 700W of solar, charges slowly, and has only a 2-year warranty ([OutdoorPowerStations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).

**EcoFlow Delta 2 Max** is good for full-time living on lighter loads.
- About 2kWh capacity.
- Recharges 0–80% from the wall in 43 minutes.
- Expandable to 6kWh.
- Source: [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

**Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is less suited to solar-heavy RV use. It only accepts 400W of solar, which would bottleneck a larger panel array ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Choosing the solar panels

- **Don't buy more panel wattage than the station can accept.** Each unit has a solar input limit, and panels beyond it are wasted.
- **Match panels to the station's inputs.** Some stations split their solar capacity across several inputs (650W each on the R4000). Each input also has voltage limits, so check that each panel string fits them.
- **Size the array to your needs.** A 300–400W folding array refills a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). A large unit needs a rooftop array closer to its input limit.
- **Lighter setups:** a Renogy 200W foldable suitcase is a common pairing ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).

## Bottom line

- **Running AC off battery:** the DELTA Pro 3, or the R4000 if price matters most and you're comfortable with the no-return risk on sale items.
- **Everything except AC:** the BLUETTI AC200L with about 400–1,200W of panels.

The only direct buy link in my search results was the ALLPOWERS one. If you tell me which station you're leaning toward, I can search for current prices and buy links for it and matching panels.
